title: High ozone and dry air overlap was close to a time-controlled reference in two months of a North Wales experiment
abstract: We tested whether high ozone and high air drying demand coincided beyond their time schedules in a North Wales wildflower experiment. We used 1,464 complete hourly records in August and September 2021. At cutoffs of 2 kPa vapor pressure deficit and 60 ppb ozone, observed overlap was within 0.46 percentage points of an exact weekday and hour reference in all twelve month and dome comparisons. Heated-minus-ambient contrasts were within 0.42 percentage points of the reference contrasts. The heated 80 ppb residual changed sign between months. All observed shares lay within or on central 95 percent whole-day permutation reference ranges. These ranges describe rearrangements, not sampling uncertainty. Nine cutoff combinations gave residuals from -0.632 to +0.800 percentage points. The method separates clock, weekly schedule and remaining overlap terms. The same records were used in a prior campaign exposure audit; this is a new schedule-control test, not independent validation. Programmed ozone, one dome per treatment, shared ambient weather, possible source gap filling and one site-year limit inference. Plant uptake, flower effects and regional climate responses are not tested. Code, aggregate results, source hashes and external retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: Observed overlap and references with no time control, hour control, and weekday plus hour control. Blue lines give central 95 percent whole-day permutation reference ranges. These are not confidence intervals. A and H denote ambient and heated domes.

citations.reason: Same external source and inherited diagnostic cutoffs. This study adds schedule controls with new code. Hourly records overlap fully in the tested months; not independent replication.
